nonNative.answer: Smoke testing is quick and shallow check of most critical path, like login and checkout, it run on every new build for decide if build is enough stable to test more. Regression testing is run again much bigger set of existing tests after change, for make sure the features what worked before still working. So smoke is fast gate run first, regression is more broad and deep and it catch side effects of the changes.

Test pyramid is saying we should have many fast and cheap unit tests in bottom, more small layer of integration or API tests in middle, and only few end to end UI tests on top. Lower layers are more fast, more stable and show failure more exact; UI tests are slow and brittle, so we use them only for critical user journey. If you invert it like ice-cream cone, pipeline become slow and flaky.

Severity is how much impact have the bug on system or user, for example crash or data loss is critical. Priority is how urgent we must fix it, this is business decision. They can be different: typo in company name on home page is low severity but high priority, and crash in admin report what nobody use often can be high severity but lower priority.
